title: Timbales (shallow drums and cowbell)
summary: Timbales are a pair of shallow metal-shelled drums on a stand, with a cowbell mounted between them. Played with thin sticks on the heads and on the shells, they drive the dance bands of Cuba with sharp, ringing patterns.
howToPlay: Two drums stand side by side, the low one on the left and the high one on the right, with a cowbell above and between them.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
The steel shell of the high drum, the paila, gives a ringing click, and the cowbell marks the bar.
Learn the shell pattern first, then add the drums.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count eight pulses, split 3 + 3 + 2.
heritageNote: In Cuban dance music the timbalero plays a steady pattern on the shell, switches to the cowbell for the loud sections, and fills between with the drums. The drums were adapted from the orchestral kettle drums.
credits: Tradition: the timbales; patterns written for this game
